close_reason: Ack. Positive finding — no code change. The 'no baked-in trust data' stance is correctly defended in lib.rs:12-25 and README.md, and matches AGENTS.md's documented stance. Recording closure as a decision-history entry; if a future contributor proposes one of the rejected refactors, this bead's reasoning is the rebuttal.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:12-25 and README.md:5-15 lay out the "no compiled-in Mozilla CA bundle, no platform integration in this crate" stance, with crisp reasoning: trust data is deployment configuration, library version cadence is the wrong coupling for it.

What a contributor might incorrectly suggest:
  - "Why not add a `mozilla` feature flag that pulls in webpki-roots equivalent?" — explicitly rejected; the README captures why (Mozilla list pins to the library release cadence; deployment-config decision wearing library clothing).
  - "Why not at least probe /etc/ssl/certs by default?" — that is pkix-truststore-system's job (PKIX-8h87). Doing it here couples Tier-1 plumbing to platform discovery.
  - "from_der_iter is overkill, just take a Vec<Vec<u8>>." — the iterator-of-bytes shape is what adapter crates need so they can stream from PKCS#11 / OS keychain APIs without pre-collecting. The IntoIterator+AsRef<[u8]> bounds are correct.

Defense: this is the right shape for the Tier-1 layer; the policy/scope concerns it raises are well-articulated and should not be relitigated without coordinating with PKIX-8h87 and PKIX-p8vz.
title: No baked-in trust data is correctly defended in the API surface
